# The appointments Auðhumla made — and who is keeping them

One myth is a story. A cycle of myths is a specification. Read Auðhumla's cycle in order and the industries fall out of it one by one.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Auðhumla
- **Pantheon:** Norse
- **Domain of influence:** Primeval Cow, Nourisher of Creation
- **Pattern seats:** 5
- **Sectors touched:** Energy & Natural World · Culture & Entertainment · Home & Lifestyle · Commerce & Governance · Society & Spirit
- **Strongest seat:** Agriculture, Food & Harvest
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 53 of 406

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest — through *The Cow in the Void*

Snorri tells how the rivers of Élivágar, flowing out of Niflheim, hardened into ice in Ginnungagap.  When the heat of Múspell met that ice, it melted and dripped; from the drips came Ymir, the first frost giant.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The primeval cow whose milk fed the first giant; dairy and nourishment at the dawn of the world.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

### Mythic Name Restoration — through *Búri Emerges*

On the first day that Auðhumla licked the stones, a man's hair came forth by evening; on the second day, a head; on the third day, the whole man stood free.  He was called Búri.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The primeval cow of Norse cosmogony, licking the first god from the ice; the restored Auðhumla keeps the eth and length.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

### Food & Hospitality — through *Two Lines from One Source*

Auðhumla stands at the branching point of the Norse cosmos.  Ymir, fed by her milk, begets the race of frost giants; Búri, freed by her licking, begins the race of gods.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The primeval cow whose milk nourished creation; dairy and abundance at the first table.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

### Ancestry & Heritage Services — through *The Cow in the Void*

Snorri tells how the rivers of Élivágar, flowing out of Niflheim, hardened into ice in Ginnungagap.  When the heat of Múspell met that ice, it melted and dripped; from the drips came Ymir, the first frost giant.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The primeval nourisher; from her milk the first giant grew and the gods were licked from the ice.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Auðhumla has only one extended scene in Norse mythology, but it is the scene from which everything else follows.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

The atlas is not a horoscope. Seats are earned from the sources — argued, weighted, published — and every one of them can be challenged at the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). A match that cannot survive an argument does not survive review. That is the whole trick: the patterns are claims, and claims can be tested.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in agriculture, food & harvest, mythic name restoration, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/audhumla/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
